pl-l4d43c6-d1e115.summary: Asks whether those whom Christ finds alive will never die, or will pass to immortality with wonderful speed at the very moment they are caught up to meet him; one should not say it is impossible that, carried aloft through the air, they die and revive in that space.

pl-l4d43c6-d1e121.summary: States that the Apostle seems to urge the view that in a short space they will suffer death and receive immortality, where he says all will be made alive in Christ, and what you sow is not made alive unless it first dies.
claims: Paul suggests the living will die and rise in the rapture.

pl-l4d43c6-d1e136.summary: Continues Augustine: why should it seem incredible that this multitude of bodies is sown in the air and immediately revives immortal and incorruptible, when we believe the resurrection happens in the twinkling of an eye and the dust of ancient corpses returns so swiftly to unending members? Yet I would rather hear more learned men. If the saints found alive pass from mortal bodies and return to them immortal in that rapture, Paul's words cause no difficulty: all will rise, good and bad, but not all will be changed to the glory of the resurrection.
claims: Instant death and resurrection in the rapture are possible.
All will rise, but only the good will be changed to glory.

pl-l4d43c6-d1e162.summary: Cites Ambrose: in the very rapture of those found alive there will be death and resurrection, the soul going out of the body as in sleep and being restored to it in a moment.
claims: Death and resurrection occur in the rapture.

pl-l4d43c6-d1e171.summary: Notes that Jerome, writing to Marcella, seems to testify to the contrary that some found alive at the end of the world will not die but be suddenly changed into immortality.
claims: Jerome seems to say the living will be changed without dying.

pl-l4d43c6-d1e180.summary: Concludes that which of these is truer is not for human judgment to define.
claims: The question is beyond human judgment.

pl-l4d43c6.summary: Asks whether those Christ finds alive will never die, or will pass to immortality at the instant of being caught up. Augustine finds it possible that they die and revive in that brief space, as Paul's 'all will be made alive' and 'what you sow is not made alive unless it dies' suggest, and as the resurrection happens in the twinkling of an eye, though he would rather hear more learned men; so all will rise, good and bad, but not all will be changed to glory. Ambrose agrees that death and resurrection occur in the rapture; Jerome seems to say some will not die but be changed. Which is truer is not for human judgment to define.
claims: Those alive at Christ's coming may die and rise instantly in the rapture.
Jerome seems to say they will be changed without dying.
The question cannot be decided by human judgment.
